page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256gb is a high-memory cloud compute instance in the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical AMD EPYC processor cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 extensions (with VNNI and BF16 support), cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI, and AMD SVM virtualization. The instance provides 256 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio tailored for memory-intensive workloads.

Benchmark results demonstrate competitive single-core and memory throughput. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2,752 and a multi-core score of 23,765, both ranking in the top tier. Memory subsystem performance is strong, registering 293.49 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 196.72 GB/sec in large-block write operations, complemented by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,068.77. In data processing tasks, single-threaded gzip compression reached 40.57 GB/sec, while in-memory throughput reached 63.76 million Redis SET operations per second.

Hardware tradeoffs center around storage allocation. The configuration includes 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and lacks local GPU hardware, necessitating external network-attached volumes for large datasets. From a resource perspective, the high RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers distinct operational density for memory-bound applications without requiring over-provisioning of processor cores.

Due to its 256 GB memory footprint and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, the vx1-m-32c-256gb is designed for in-memory caching layers, Redis clusters, large database instances, Clang-based software compilation, and ETL batch processing pipelines that require substantial memory bandwidth.
description: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256gb is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance powered by 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical AMD EPYC cores at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 256 GB of system RAM, it maintains an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suited for data-heavy operations. Benchmark testing demonstrates strong memory throughput, registering 196.72 GB/sec in uncached block writes and a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,068.77, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 2,752 and multi-core score of 23,765. The instance bundles 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and contains no discrete GPUs, necessitating external volumes for persistent high-capacity storage. With strong in-memory key-value processing reaching 63.76 million Redis SET operations per second, this server is suitable for in-memory databases, caching tiers, analytics data pipelines, and large software build environments.
